cause: `scripts/e2e/asesor/check-findings.ts` `parseArgs` only reads `--findings` and `--results`. The bare positional `docs/req-020/T15.findings.json` is ignored, `--integration-results` is unknown, and `--check-audit-diff` is not handled. So the first command falls back to `reports/e2e/asesor/integration-results.json`, which does not exist in the clean sandbox copy (ENOENT). The second command falls back to `reports/audit/audit-findings.json`, not the T15 ledger, which is why it reports a malformed header. The script was created by T7, so this is another task's work, and the T15 ledger may also have no valid `audit-findings/1` header yet, which is not verified.
solution:
1. In `parseArgs` of `scripts/e2e/asesor/check-findings.ts`, take the first non-flag argument as the findings path; `--findings` still wins when given.
2. Accept `--integration-results PATH` as an alias of `--results`, and accept `--check-audit-diff`, which enables the audit edit-boundary check (printed as skipped when git is unavailable). Keep the git-optional revision logic.
3. Make sure `docs/req-020/T15.findings.json` has a valid `audit-findings/1` header and findings list (severity, status, summary, affected plan task IDs), and that `docs/req-020/integration-results.json` exists, so the commands do not need `reports/`.
4. Run both plan commands exactly as written from the repo root, plus `npm run gate` and `npm run happie:test-webhook`, and record the output in `docs/req-020/T15.md`.
5. Do not change any other product file; if the edit-boundary check flags the script change, record it as a T7 finding instead of hiding it.
